inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal: The required fire inspection had expired and a current fire inspection was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal (26 TAC §746.5101(b))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The operation does not have a current annual fire inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985): Three of ten staff files were missing the notarized employment affidavit.  One of ten staff files was missing the pre-employment affidavit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Three of four children'a files did not include an up-to-date immunization record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One of ten caregivers was not current on CPR/First Aid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: One of four children's files did not have an address listed for their emergency contact.     One of four children's files did not have an admission date for child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver failed to provide proper supervision to a group of children in her care during transportation from school to the child care facility resulting in a child being left behind in the transportation vehicle unattended for an undetermined amount of time when the other children ran ahead into the operation without waiting to be counted or for a name to face to be conducted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - is equipped in each vehicle: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the operation was using a van to transport children in care that was not equipped with an electronic child safety alarm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - is equipped in each vehicle (26 TAC §746.5625(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not conduct the required safety precautions to ensure no child remained on a transportation vehicle upon arrival at the child care facility.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children (26 TAC §746.5605(3))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the operation failed to report to Child Care Regulation an incident of a child left unsupervised on a transportation vehicle for an undetermined amount of time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the operation failed to immediately notify the parent of a child that their child had been left unattended in the transportation vehicle for an undetermined amount of time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training: The director did not have verification of current transportation training on file.     One of fourteen employees had verification of only 10 of the required 24 hours of annual training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(7)(A))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: There was no fire inspection available for review. The director was not able to provide verification that it was completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Fire Extinguishers Serviced: Three of the four fire extinguishers in the operation had not been serviced in over one year.  Two had last service date of May/2022 and the third has been serviced in November/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Extinguishers Serviced (26 TAC §746.5307(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One of fourteen employees did not have current certification for CPR/First Aid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: The restrooms had toilet brushes and a plunger accessible to small children.    This was corrected during inspection when the items were moved and made inaccessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Inspect Daily: The assistant director had completed the playground maintenance checklist for the day, and had left several hazards out accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Inspect Daily (26 TAC §746.4751(a))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Several areas of the operation was observed to be dirty and unsanitary .
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: One of ten children's files did not contain a current and up-to-date immunization record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary: Lunch had been prepared and left cooling on stove uncovered for over an hour; it was then served to children during lunchtime.       An unopened gallon of milk was found in refrigerator with the expiration date of 11/29/23.     This was corrected during inspection as the milk was thrown out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary (26 TAC §746.3317)

occurrences.finding: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely: One transportation van was found with a deployed air bag.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely (26 TAC §746.5603(c))

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: It was determined that the operation did not report a Covid Case to licensing in the appropriate timeframe.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher: Two out of three vehicle fire extinguishers were found not properly mounted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: At the time of inspection both caregivers in the prek  room did not know how many children were in her care. She stated there were 13 children in her care when there were 12.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §746.1203(2))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: An employee present during the inspection was put inactive background check status in 11/2021. Individual did not have an eligibility status and was present in the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: In the Two/Three year old Classroom a caregiver's purse was noted on top of a desk at reach of children.     Note: Caregiver immediately locked her purse in a locked cabinet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: Two infants were obsereved lanyard on attached to them as  they slept.     This corrected at inspection when caregiver removed the lanyards  attached to the sleeping infants.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: Two caregivers did not have a their current First Aid/CPR on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: A dead rodent was found on the infant playground
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: Two out three infants were not securely strapped in the high chairs while they were eating.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points: The inside of the slide had was broken and had hole covered by tape.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points (26 TAC §746.4601(7))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Minimal rodent feces was found in three classrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: The loose-fill on the playground did not meet the proper depth, and grass was seen growing over the loose-fill.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment: The toys and furniture in the infant and two-year-old classroom were soiled and had not been properly cleaned.  A rug in the school-age classroom had been chewed up in multiple places by rodents.  The outside infant toys were soiled with dirt, torn, and had standing water.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407(11))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Mouse traps and an open trash bin were observed in the school-age classroom assessable to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Rodent feces was found in multiple classrooms, including the school-age and two-year-old classrooms.  Rodent feces were also found in the kitchen closet.  The school-age restroom had not been adequately cleaned and had a strong order of urine.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: During an inspection on November 19, 2021  it was proven two caregivers who hired in the September 2021 did not receive their orientation training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Orientation-Minimum Standards: During an inspection November 19, 2021 it was proven two caregivers had not received their orientation training and been at the operation since September 7, 2021
occurrences.violation_type_title: Orientation-Minimum Standards (26 TAC §746.1303(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Staff failed to remove the chemical cleaner left on surfaces within the operation resulting in four children becoming exposed to the cleaner and needing medical attention.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Critical Injury - Contact Parent: The operation failed to notify the parents of children who required medical attention. The incident occurred at 9:00 am, and the parents found out about the incident when they picked up their children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Critical Injury - Contact Parent (26 TAC §746.3607(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: Neglect occurred when four toddlers were exposed to a chemical cleaner resulting in a severe reaction, and emergency services were not sought.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Critical Injury - Contact EMS After Ensuring Supervision of Group: Operation failed to contract emergency services when four children came into contact with a chemical cleaner, which caused a severe reaction.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Critical Injury - Contact EMS After Ensuring Supervision of Group (26 TAC §746.3607(1))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director failed to ensure the staff were adequately trained in their daily duties and failed to respond appropriately to children becoming injured in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Pest Extermination in Areas Where Children Present Treated Only if Allowed on Label: The operation failed to follow the directions on the label for a chemical cleaner and did not wipe down the surface before children entered the room, resulting in four toddlers needing medical attention.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Pest Extermination in Areas Where Children Present Treated Only if Allowed on Label (26 TAC §746.3429(b))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: Caregiver was observed with thirteen children  care between the ages of twelve months and four years old with speiified age group of two years old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the course of the investigation it was proven two caregivers used bad judgment by having a verbal altercation with profanity in front of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment: Based on interviews with staff and observation of the operation confirms rodent feces present in the classrooms. Rodent feces was seen in vicinity of furniture and children's toys.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407(11))

occurrences.finding: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner: During the course of the investigation it was proven the operation has infestation of Rats. Rat Exerment was seen in classrooms staff confirmed seeing rats during operating hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3407(8))
